children: Effective 1 December 2026, the leadership transition will see Grey 82.5 CEO Ramamurthy succeed Baruah, who moves to lead VML’s Ford business across the region

VML India has announced a leadership transition, with Kiran Ramamurthy set to take over as Chief Executive Officer (CEO) from Babita Baruah, effective 1 December 2026. Baruah will move into a senior regional leadership role as Head of the Ford business, as the agency looks to sustain growth, creative innovation and client partnerships.

Baruah brings more than three decades of industry experience, including two decades working with major brands such as The Coca-Cola Company, Unilever, Nestlé and Kellogg’s. Before taking charge of VML India, she was based in Bangkok as Regional Client Lead for the Ford International Market Group and Executive Director at VMLY&R Thailand.

During her tenure at VML India, Baruah has overseen business performance and creative work recognised at platforms including Cannes Lions and the Effies. In her new role, she will focus on developing VML’s Ford business across the region.
Ramamurthy To Drive VML India’s Next Phase

Ramamurthy, currently CEO of Grey 82.5, brings more than 30 years of experience across mainline advertising, design, technology and content production. His portfolio includes work with brands such as Unilever, Amazon, Toyota, IBM, Coca-Cola, ITC, De Beers and Tata Consumer Products.

He has also been involved in developing centralised marketing services in India through the Lenovo Marketing Hub. At 82.5, Ramamurthy led transformation and growth, including the integration of Grey and 82.5.

Commenting on the appointments, Hephzibah Pathak, CEO of WPP Creative India, says, “The leadership transitions reflect our commitment to nurturing exceptional talent across our network while maintaining absolute continuity and momentum for our clients. VML enters this next chapter in a position of strength, backed by strong operational and creative achievements over the past year.

Babita has done a tremendous job steering VML India, and her elevation to lead the Ford business regionally is a well-deserved recognition of her international leadership. In Kiran, VML gains a dynamic leader whose diverse experience, operational acumen, and creative hunger make him exceptionally well-suited to drive the agency's vision. I look forward to Kiran’s dynamic leadership to take the agency into its next chapter while celebrating Babita’s continued impact across the region.”
The transition reflects VML’s focus on leadership mobility within its network, with Ramamurthy taking charge of the India business and Baruah moving into a regional role overseeing the Ford account.
